solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: A large bay or a roomy one? (6)

blocks.note: kept as it stands
L = large, as on clothing labels
a cove is a small bay

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a stretch of coastline is a great bay or merely a spacious one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roomy' is the pun: not spacious but belonging to a room, so 'a roomy one' is a bay inside a room.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on 'roomy': an alcove is a bay or recess set into the wall of a room.

entries.clue: What solicitor does: bill charges (6)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes the action; the answer is the bare verb for it.

blocks.note: AC = account, a bill
cost = charge, the price asked

annotation.surface: A note on a lawyer's work: sending out the bill for fees.
annotation.walkthrough: The solicitor here is not a lawyer but a prostitute, who solicits by approaching strangers in the street.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: to accost is to approach a stranger boldly, which is what a streetwalker soliciting does.

entries.clue: Thoroughly search local, not initially confrontational (9)

indicatorNotes.not initially: 'not initially' means minus what comes first, so the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
NATIVE (local) without its N

annotation.surface: Advice to scour the neighbourhood pub, which turns out to be a hostile place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Local' is also British slang for a neighbourhood pub, but here it is the adjective: a native of the area is local.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone combative is eager to fight or argue, i.e. confrontational.

entries.clue: Boast unit has avoided 50 per cent in tax (5)

indicatorNotes.has avoided 50 per cent: to avoid half of something is to escape half of it, so half the word's letters go missing
indicatorNotes.in: 'in tax' puts the reduced word inside the tax, as money is held in an account

blocks.note: UNIT with half its letters (IT) gone
VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax; UN goes between VA and T

annotation.surface: A business brags about having dodged half of what it owed in tax.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface boast is about tax dodging; the definition is simply the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to vaunt something is to brag about it, from the same root as 'vain'.

entries.clue: Special importance of piano in arrangement of Messiah (8)

indicatorNotes.arrangement of: a musical arrangement reworks a piece, and here the letters themselves are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: p = piano, soft in musical notation; it goes 'in' with the other letters
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A critic praises how prominent the piano is in a new arrangement of Handel's Messiah.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'arrangement' look like an orchestration; it is the instruction to rearrange MESSIAH plus P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting stress on something marks it out as especially important.

entries.clue: Kinsmen use boys to run underhand dealings (6,8)

indicatorNotes.to run: letters that are sent to run are set loose, and they come back in a different order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A family firm sends its young lads out to carry out shady deals.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface already describes a family racket, so the definition sits comfortably at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: monkey business is mischievous or dishonest activity, like a monkey's tricks.

entries.clue: Shortly permitted to stuff bird, as there may be a party tonight? (9)

annotation.definition: as there may be a party tonight?

indicatorNotes.Shortly: said shortly, a word is clipped, so it loses its final letter
indicatorNotes.to stuff: stuffing a bird means packing filling inside it, so the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: ALLOWED without its final D
a hen is a bird; ALLOWE goes between H and EN

annotation.surface: Someone is allowed to stuff a chicken because guests are coming round this evening.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint rather than a synonym: on 31 October, the night itself is Halloween, a night known for parties.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: Halloween night is famous for costume parties, so it is a night when there may well be one.

entries.clue: Seafood I cooked with peas (5)

indicatorNotes.cooked: cooking changes the form of the ingredients, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Someone describes a dish they made: seafood with peas.
annotation.walkthrough: SEPIA is best known as a brown colour, which is why the seafood sense is hard to see.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: sepia is the cuttlefish, eaten as seafood, and the source of the brown ink named after it.

entries.clue: Joined and served in the army, having lost heart (8)

indicatorNotes.having lost heart: a word's heart is its middle letter, and losing heart removes it

blocks.clueFragment: served in the army, having lost heart
blocks.note: SOLDIERED without its middle letter I

annotation.surface: A man enlisted and did his military service, but came back demoralised.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joined' reads as enlisting, which chimes with the army; it is the definition, meaning fastened together.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific sense: soldering is one way of joining metal parts, with melted alloy.

entries.clue: What might be played in saloon car shared by baseball team? (4,4,6)

indicatorNotes.shared by: a car shared by the team belongs to them, which the possessive 'S expresses

blocks.note: a baseball team is nine men, and the car is theirs: NINE MEN'S
Morris is an old British car maker, whose models included saloons

annotation.surface: A question about what game gets played in a car the baseball team shares.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a bar, where games are played, but it is a saloon car. Nine men's morris is an ancient board game played with nine pieces each.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: nine men's morris is a board game, so it is something that might be played.

entries.clue: Not unusual to secure college fellowship (9)

indicatorNotes.to secure: to secure something is to hold it safely enclosed, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: common = not unusual
uni = university, a college; it sits inside COMM-ON

annotation.surface: It is quite normal for a college to award someone a research fellowship.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'fellowship' as an academic post, which suits the college; the definition means companionship.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: communion is shared fellowship, as in being 'in communion with' others.

entries.clue: Flap as clumsy oaf falls into lake after lake (5)

indicatorNotes.falls into: something that falls into a place ends up inside it, so the oaf lands between the two lakes

blocks.note: L = lake, twice
a clumsy oaf is an ape; it goes between the two Ls

annotation.surface: Panic as a clumsy man stumbles into one lake after another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like panic in the surface; it is the definition, a folded piece of cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a lapel is the folded-back flap on the front of a jacket.

entries.clue: Resort mail, unwanted mostly (3)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: SPAM, unwanted email, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Holiday mail from a resort is mostly junk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mail, unwanted' is spam, the junk that fills an inbox.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a spa town is a resort built around mineral springs.

entries.clue: Your position located: success! (5,3,3)

blocks.note: said when you have been found: that is where you are
said when something has been done: there, it works

annotation.surface: A satnav pinpoints where you are and announces success.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves are everyday exclamations: one on finding someone, one on finishing a task.
annotation.definitionFit: Two idioms: 'There you are!' means both 'I've found you' and 'done, just as I said'.

entries.clue: Run through offer that is something players of course want (6)

indicatorNotes.through: a run that goes through the offer passes inside it, ending up between its letters

blocks.note: a bid is an offer
R = run, as on a cricket scorecard; it goes into BI-D
i.e. = id est, that is

annotation.surface: Players naturally want someone to run through an offer with them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally'; read literally it means 'on the course', i.e. golfers.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one under par on a hole is what golfers want on the course.

entries.clue: Gives diet out relating to processing of food (9)

indicatorNotes.out: letters that are out are knocked out of place, so they come back in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A nutritionist hands out diet plans about how food is processed.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about food, so the fodder and the definition look like one sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: digestion is the body's processing of food, and this adjective relates to it.

entries.clue: Take the air, on going in to swim (7)

indicatorNotes.going in to: going in to something means entering it, so the first piece enters the second

blocks.note: to bathe is to swim
re = on, concerning; it goes inside B-ATHE

annotation.surface: Someone takes a breath of air before plunging in for a swim.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take the air' usually means going for a stroll; here it is literal, drawing air in.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom read literally: to take the air usually means a stroll, but breathing is literally taking air in.

entries.clue: Several months sewing border into canopy (9)

indicatorNotes.sewing: sewing one piece of cloth onto another fixes it in place, here inside the canopy
indicatorNotes.into: 'into' directs where the sewn piece goes: inside the next word

blocks.note: a rim is a border
a tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed; RIM goes after its T

annotation.surface: A seamstress spends months stitching a trim onto a canopy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sewing border' suggests TRIM or HEM, but the border is RIM and the T comes from TESTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A precise sense: a trimester is three months, the usual stage of a pregnancy or school year.

entries.clue: Inclined to scorn attitude taken by daughter (8)

indicatorNotes.taken by: the daughter takes the pose in hand, so D follows it

blocks.note: to dis someone is to scorn them
a pose is an attitude struck
D = daughter, as in family trees; it comes after POSE

annotation.surface: A daughter adopts a pose of contempt and is inclined to sneer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inclined to' looks like it runs on into 'scorn'; the 'to' is a link and 'Inclined' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being disposed to do something means leaning or inclined that way.

entries.clue: One wise man is heard in long periods (3,4)

indicatorNotes.heard: what is heard is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: I = one and a sage is a wise man, so the phrase is heard as 'I, sage, is'

annotation.surface: A wise man's voice carries down through the ages.
annotation.walkthrough: The word breaks fall in different places: 'I sage is' said quickly runs into 'ice ages'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the glacial eras lasted many thousands of years, and the phrase is used loosely for any very long time.

entries.clue: Wrong people close to you are understood (4,2)

annotation.definitionNote: The plural 'are understood' matches 'these things sink in'.

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
your kin are your relatives

annotation.surface: Wrongdoers you are close to are forgiven because they are understood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' looks like an adjective in the surface; it is the noun, a sin.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: when news sinks in it is finally grasped, as if soaking into the mind.

entries.clue: Ancient city blessed hosts on a regular basis (6)

indicatorNotes.hosts: a host takes guests in, so the blessed word holds the city inside it

blocks.note: holy = blessed
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city; it goes inside HO-LY

annotation.surface: An ancient holy city regularly takes in pilgrims.
annotation.walkthrough: UR is the crossword's favourite ancient city.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: things done every hour recur at a fixed interval, one kind of regular basis.

entries.clue: Liberal rector opens part of abbey (5,6)

indicatorNotes.Liberal: a liberal reading is a free one, so the letters are free to move

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A broad-minded vicar opens up part of the abbey to visitors.
annotation.walkthrough: Poets' Corner is the part of Westminster Abbey in London where many writers are buried or remembered.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this corner of the south transept of Westminster Abbey is one part of an abbey.

entries.clue: One dumped manuscript containing answer papers (5)

indicatorNotes.containing: a container holds something inside it, so MS holds the A

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner, someone dumped
MS = manuscript
A = answer; it goes inside MS

annotation.surface: A jilted lover finds a manuscript full of papers answering them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Papers' is the school sense: exams are also called papers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: in British schools a test is often called a paper.

entries.clue: Horse circling wide tree (5)

indicatorNotes.circling: a horse circling something runs all the way round it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat
W = wide, a cricket scoring term; it goes inside RO-AN

annotation.surface: A horse runs a wide circle round a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: W for wide is from cricket, where a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the mountain ash, with its red berries, is one particular tree.

entries.clue: I say “Love” (3)

blocks.note: e.g. = for example, say
O = love, a zero score in tennis

annotation.surface: Someone declares love out loud.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like a British exclamation; 'I' is the definition and 'say' is e.g.
annotation.definitionFit: A translation: the Latin for 'I', used in English for the self.

entries.clue: One’s holding in stomach around teacher (5)

indicatorNotes.holding in: to hold something in is to keep it inside, as you hold in your stomach
indicatorNotes.around: to turn around is to face the other way, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: one is = I + 'S; the two letters take MAW between them
a maw is an animal's stomach, giving I-MAW-S

annotation.surface: Someone sucks their stomach in round the teacher.
annotation.walkthrough: The container IMAWS is built first, then 'around' turns the whole thing back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific sense: a Hindu religious teacher or master is one particular kind of teacher.

entries.clue: At first rub over with brine, not a perfume (4,5)

indicatorNotes.At first: at first means at the very start, so only the opening letter counts
indicatorNotes.not a: 'not a' tells the word to do without an A, so one A is dropped

blocks.note: first letter of rub
O = over, a cricket term
SEAWATER (brine) without its A

annotation.surface: Instructions to begin by rubbing something over with salt water, which is not a perfume.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not a perfume' looks like a comment on brine; 'not a' is the deletion and 'perfume' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: water scented with rose petals is a light perfume.

entries.clue: Regularly ties up thick boxes to distribute (8)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
indicatorNotes.boxes: to box something is to enclose it, so the thick word goes round the letters

blocks.note: dense = thick
tIeS uP, the even letters; they go inside D-ENSE

annotation.surface: Someone ties up thick boxes to send them out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up' is not a direction here: it supplies the P as part of the letters taken regularly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hand or share out, as a pharmacist does with medicine.

entries.clue: Nastily scornful, like a creature hunted in fits? (6)

annotation.definition2: like a creature hunted in fits?

blocks.note: sarcastically critical, with a sneer

blocks.clueFragment: like a creature hunted in fits?
blocks.note: the Snark is the beast of Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark

annotation.surface: Someone is cruelly scornful, like a hunted animal lashing out in fits.
annotation.walkthrough: Carroll's poem The Hunting of the Snark is subtitled An Agony in Eight Fits, 'fit' being an old word for a section of a poem.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain sense plus a playful one: sarcastic and sneering, and also resembling Carroll's Snark.
